key_insight: Sufficiently capable frozen LLM agents can devise their own context-based self-improvement strategies without a prescribed learning loop.
engineering_relevance: Agent systems may improve through autonomous experimentation and editable text memory without updating model weights.
method: Provide a frozen LLM with a compute budget, basic tools, and a general self-improvement goal.
Let it collect gameplay experience and update text documents without an externally imposed loop or real-world data.
Evaluate whether learned text artifacts transfer to external benchmarks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports gameplay self-improvement and transfer gains across different game horizons, mechanics, and 3D navigation, but provides no quantitative results.
watch_item: Success depends on model capability, and the abstract does not establish reliability or compute efficiency beyond the tested settings.
paper_title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
